title: esri-tilecache: open Esri tile caches as GeoPackage and MBTiles without re-encoding
description:
Problem. National maps are distributed as Esri tile packages. A national forest map used in our work comes from a state agency as a single .tpk of several GB stored as Compact Cache V1. Open GIS software and mobile field apps cannot use it directly.

State as of 23 November 2026. GDAL — and with it QGIS — reads .tpkx and Compact V2 caches, but not the older Compact V1 .tpk, still used by some national mapping agencies; the V1 layout is not documented by Esri. The alternatives were proprietary software or re-encoding the tiles with quality loss.

Solution. This package reads all of them, keeps every image tile byte for byte (no quality loss, conversion limited only by disk speed) and writes a GeoPackage that GDAL, QGIS and mobile apps open directly; LERC elevation caches become float32 coverages and vector tile packages MBTiles. The undocumented V1 layout is described in METHODOLOGY.md. The QGIS plugin Esri Tile Cache Converter offers the same conversion in QGIS.

Aim. National maps distributed as Esri tile packages should be usable in open GIS software and offline on mobile devices in forest field work, without loss of quality and with an open, verifiable method.
